seed: A seed is the small, hard part of a plant that a new plant grows from.

meet: When you meet someone, you see them and talk to them.

sea: The sea is the large area of salty water that covers much of the earth.

window: A window is a space in a wall, filled with glass, that lets light in.
tie: When you tie something, you fasten it with a knot or a bow.

hit: If you hit something, you touch it hard with your hand or with an object.

both: You use both to talk about two people or things together.
inside: If you go inside, you go into a building or a room.
forget: If you forget something, you do not remember it.
witch: A witch is a woman in stories who has magic powers.
fear: Fear is the feeling you have when you think something bad might happen.
grow: When something grows, it gets bigger.
pull: When you pull something, you hold it and move it towards you.
wing: A wing is one of the two parts of a bird's or an insect's body that it uses for flying.
empty: Something that is empty has nothing inside it.
slide: A slide is a smooth, sloping piece of equipment in a playground that children slide down.
roar: When a lion roars, it makes a very loud, deep sound.
napkin: A napkin is a piece of cloth or paper that you use at meals to wipe your mouth and hands.
soon: Soon means in a short time from now.
present: A present is something that you give to someone, for example on their birthday.
voice: Your voice is the sound you make when you speak or sing.
moon: The moon is the round object that moves around the earth and shines in the sky at night.
drawing: A drawing is a picture made with a pencil, a pen or a crayon.
darkness: Darkness is when there is no light.
wipe: When you wipe something, you clean it by rubbing it with a cloth.
unicorn: A unicorn is a magical white horse in stories with a horn on its head.
snowy: When the weather is snowy, it snows a lot.
share: When you share something, you let someone else have some of it or use it too.
size: The size of something is how big or small it is.
horn: A horn is the part of a car or a bus that you press to make a loud warning noise. Some animals, such as goats, have horns on their heads.
beard: A beard is the hair that grows on a man's chin and cheeks.
some: You use some to talk about an amount of something without saying exactly how much.
sure: If you are sure about something, you know it is true.
line: A line is a long, thin mark. A line of people is a row of them.
bat: A bat is a small animal like a mouse with wings that flies at night. A bat is also a piece of wood for hitting a ball.
they: You use they to talk about two or more people or things.
far: If something is far away, it is a long way away.
dream: A dream is the pictures and events that you see in your mind while you are asleep.
kind: Someone who is kind is friendly and helps other people.
hope: If you hope that something will happen, you want it to happen.
ground: The ground is the surface of the earth that you walk on.
blood: Blood is the red liquid that flows around your body.
piece: A piece of something is a part of it.
write: When you write, you put letters and words on paper or on a screen.
reach: When you reach for something, you stretch out your arm to touch it.
shut: When you shut something, you close it.
medicine: Medicine is something that you take to help you get better when you are ill.
bunch: A bunch is a group of things held together, such as flowers or grapes.
wire: A wire is a long, thin piece of metal like a string. Wires carry electricity.
tear: A tear is a drop of salty water that comes out of your eye when you cry.
dish: A dish is a bowl or plate for cooking or serving food. A dish is also food cooked in a special way.
gentle: Someone who is gentle is kind and careful and does not hurt anyone.
thunder: Thunder is the loud, rumbling noise that you hear in the sky during a storm.
liar: A liar is someone who tells lies.
ankle: Your ankle is the part of your body where your foot joins your leg.
sour: Something that is sour has a sharp taste, like a lemon.
them: You use them to talk about two or more people or things, after a verb or after a word like to or with.
very: You use very to make a word stronger.
behind: If something is behind another thing, it is at the back of it.
huge: Something that is huge is very, very big.
river: A river is a long line of water that flows across the land into the sea.
bush: A bush is a plant like a small tree with lots of branches.
naughty: A child who is naughty behaves badly.
this: You use this to talk about a person or thing that is near you.
down: If something goes down, it moves to a lower place.
woods: Woods are a large area of land covered with trees.
alone: If you are alone, nobody else is with you.
storm: A storm is very bad weather with strong winds and heavy rain.
string: String is thin rope made of twisted threads.
mouse: A mouse is a small furry animal with a long tail.
only: You use only to say that there is nothing more or nobody else.
place: A place is a building, an area or a town.
each: You use each to talk about every person or thing in a group, one by one.
woman: A woman is a grown-up female person.
daughter: Someone's daughter is their female child.
driver: A driver is a person who drives a car, a bus or a lorry.
tall: Someone or something that is tall is very high.
cousin: Your cousin is the child of your aunt or your uncle.
bow: A bow is a knot with two loops that you use for tying ribbons and shoelaces.
fold: When you fold something, you bend it so that one part lies on top of another.
curtain: A curtain is a piece of cloth that hangs at a window.
mustard: Mustard is a yellow sauce with a strong, hot taste.
rinse: When you rinse something, you wash it in clean water.
once: If something happens once, it happens one time.
its: You use its to show that something belongs to a thing or an animal.
could: You use could to say that someone was able to do something, or to ask for something politely.
open: When you open something, you move it so that it is not closed.
special: Something that is special is different from usual and better.
stuff: Stuff is an informal word for things.
loss: Loss is when you lose something.
fix: When you fix something that is broken, you mend it.
roof: The roof is the top covering of a building.
harm: If you harm someone or something, you hurt or damage them.
shadow: A shadow is a dark shape that appears when something blocks the light.
spin: When something spins, it turns round and round very quickly.
easter: Easter is a spring festival when Christians celebrate Jesus coming back to life. Many children get chocolate eggs.
pour: When you pour a liquid, you make it flow out of a container.
bee: A bee is a flying insect with yellow and black stripes that makes honey.
cheer: When people cheer, they shout loudly to show that they are happy or to encourage someone.
sadness: Sadness is the feeling of being unhappy.
swan: A swan is a large white bird with a long neck that lives on rivers and lakes.
wrestle: When people wrestle, they fight by holding each other and trying to push each other down.
torch: A torch is a small electric light that you can carry in your hand.
those: You use those to talk about people or things that are not near you.
we: You use we to talk about yourself and one or more other people.
great: Something that is great is very good.
something: Something means a thing, when you do not know or do not say what.
beauty: Beauty is the quality of being very pleasant to look at.
hole: A hole is an empty space or a gap in something.
salt: Salt is a white powder that you put on food to give it flavour.
chest: Your chest is the front part of your body between your neck and your tummy.
itch: When your skin itches, you want to scratch it.
raisin: A raisin is a dried grape.
fill: When you fill something, you put so much into it that it is full.
singer: A singer is a person who sings.
ghost: A ghost is the spirit of a dead person that some people believe they can see.

dust: Dust is very small, dry bits of dirt.
powder: Powder is lots of very tiny bits of a dry substance.
cage: A cage is a box made of bars or wire where birds or animals are kept.
neighbour: Your neighbour is someone who lives next to you or near you.
cheek: Your cheeks are the soft parts of your face below your eyes.
spit: When you spit, you push liquid out of your mouth.
about: You use about to say what something is on or what it deals with.
never: Never means not at any time.
away: If you go away, you leave a place.
her: You use her to talk about a woman, a girl or a female animal, after a verb or after a word like to or with.
careful: If you are careful, you think about what you are doing so that you do not have an accident.
throat: Your throat is the back of your mouth and the inside of your neck.
too: Too means as well. Too can also mean more than is good.
add: When you add something, you put it with something else.
bride: A bride is a woman on her wedding day.
daytime: Daytime is the part of the day when it is light.
be: You use be to say what or how someone or something is. Its forms include am, is, are, was and were.
part: A part of something is a piece of it.
feel: If you feel something, you notice it with your body or your mind.
money: Money is coins and notes that you use to buy things.
town: A town is a place with lots of houses, shops and other buildings. It is smaller than a city.
follow: If you follow someone, you go after them.
safe: If you are safe, you are not in danger.
speed: The speed of something is how fast it moves.
alive: If something is alive, it is living.
mix: When you mix things, you put them together and stir them.
prize: A prize is something that you get for winning a competition.
branch: A branch is one of the parts of a tree that grow out from the trunk.
pen: A pen is a long, thin thing that you write with in ink.
nest: A nest is a home that birds make out of twigs and grass to lay their eggs in.
camel: A camel is a large animal with one or two humps on its back that lives in the desert.
so: You use so to say what happens because of something.
child: A child is a young boy or girl.
church: A church is a building where Christians go to pray.
fat: Someone or something that is fat has a large, round body.
pool: A pool is a swimming pool or a small area of water.
time: Time is what we measure in minutes, hours and days.
married: If two people are married, they are husband and wife.
touch: When you touch something, you put your hand or fingers on it.
carry: When you carry something, you hold it and take it with you.
ink: Ink is the coloured liquid in a pen.
tent: A tent is a shelter made of cloth that you sleep in when you go camping.
pond: A pond is a small area of water.
love: If you love someone, you care about them very much. If you love something, you like it very much.
heart: Your heart is the part inside your chest that pumps blood around your body.
dead: Something that is dead is no longer alive.
choice: If you have a choice, you can decide between two or more things.
deer: A deer is a large wild animal that can run fast. The males have antlers.
swallow: When you swallow food or drink, you make it go down your throat.
bark: When a dog barks, it makes a loud, short sound.
front: The front of something is the part that faces forwards.
own: If something is your own, it belongs to you and nobody else.
free: If something is free, you do not have to pay for it.
himself: You use himself when a man or boy does something and has it done to him.
birth: Birth is the time when a baby is born.
corner: A corner is the place where two sides or edges meet.
goat: A goat is an animal with horns and a little beard that is often kept on farms.
land: Land is the part of the earth that is not covered by water.
chain: A chain is a line of metal rings joined together.
glitter: Glitter is tiny shiny pieces of paper or plastic used to decorate things.
year: A year is twelve months, from January to December.
stain: A stain is a dirty mark that is hard to get out.
prayer: A prayer is words that people say when they speak to God.
barefoot: If you are barefoot, you are not wearing anything on your feet.
their: You use their to show that something belongs to two or more people or things.
still: You use still to say that something is happening now and has not stopped.
happen: When something happens, it takes place.
drive: When you drive a car, bus or lorry, you make it go where you want.
pick: When you pick something, you choose it. You also pick flowers or fruit when you take them from a plant.
kettle: A kettle is a container with a handle and a spout that you use to boil water.
prince: A prince is the son of a king or queen.
painting: A painting is a picture that someone has made with paint.
quit: If you quit something, you stop doing it.
stomach: Your stomach is the part inside your body where food goes after you swallow it.
shake: When you shake something, you move it quickly up and down or from side to side.
would: You use would to talk about something that you imagine, or to ask for something politely.
late: If you are late, you arrive after the time you should arrive.
bottom: The bottom of something is its lowest part. Your bottom is the part of your body that you sit on.
repeat: If you repeat something, you say it or do it again.
break: If you break something, it falls into pieces or stops working.
climb: When you climb, you go up something using your hands and feet.
cloth: Cloth is material made from wool, cotton or other threads. A cloth is a piece of it that you use for cleaning.
back: Your back is the part of your body from your neck to your bottom, on the other side from your chest.
early: If you are early, you arrive before the time you should arrive.
feeling: A feeling is something that you feel, such as happiness, anger or fear.
somebody: Somebody means a person, when you do not know or do not say who.
world: The world is the Earth and all the countries and people on it.
allow: If you allow someone to do something, you let them do it.
gate: A gate is a door in a fence or wall that you open to go into a garden, field or other place.
clay: Clay is a soft, sticky kind of earth that you can shape and then bake to make pots.
needle: A needle is a thin, pointed piece of metal with a hole at one end. You use it with thread to sew.
hay: Hay is long grass that has been cut and dried. Farmers feed it to animals.
beetle: A beetle is an insect with a hard, shiny back.
other: Other means a different one, or the rest of a group.
ship: A ship is a very large boat that carries people or things across the sea.
heat: Heat is warmth, or the quality of being hot.
garden: A garden is the land next to a house where people grow grass, flowers and vegetables.
flag: A flag is a piece of cloth with a pattern on it. It is the sign of a country or group.
sheet: A sheet is a large piece of cloth that you put on a bed. A sheet of paper is one piece of paper.
jaw: Your jaw is the bottom part of your face that moves when you talk or eat.
parcel: A parcel is something wrapped in paper or put in a box so that it can be sent by post.
hall: A hall is the space just inside the front door of a house. A hall is also a big room for meetings or events.
if: You use if to talk about something that might happen.
how: You use how to ask about the way something happens or is done.
saw: A saw is a tool with a sharp edge of metal teeth that you use for cutting wood. Saw is also the past tense of see.
fifth: The fifth thing is the one that comes after the fourth.
sixth: The sixth thing is the one that comes after the fifth.
mind: Your mind is the part of you that thinks, feels and remembers.
death: Death is the end of a person's or an animal's life.
earth: The Earth is the planet that we live on. Earth is also the soil that plants grow in.
correct: Something that is correct is right and has no mistakes.
web: A web is a net of thin threads that a spider makes to catch insects.
tool: A tool is something that you hold in your hand to help you do a job, such as a hammer or a saw.
candle: A candle is a stick of wax with a string in the middle that you burn to give light.
drawer: A drawer is a box that slides in and out of a piece of furniture. You keep things in it.
cinnamon: Cinnamon is a sweet brown spice that comes from the bark of a tree.
magician: A magician is a person who does magic tricks to entertain people.
way: The way to a place is the road or path that goes there. The way you do something is how you do it.
job: A job is the work that someone does to earn money. A job is also a task.
pass: If you pass someone or something, you go past them. If you pass something to someone, you give it to them.
secret: A secret is something that only you or a few people know, and that you do not tell others.
spot: A spot is a small round mark on something. A spot is also a small red lump on your skin.
laughter: Laughter is the sound of people laughing.
float: If something floats, it stays on top of water or moves slowly through the air.
windy: If it is windy, there is a lot of wind.
listen: If you listen to something, you pay attention to a sound.
beginning: The beginning of something is the first part of it.
porch: A porch is a small covered area at the front door of a house.
handwriting: Your handwriting is the way that you write with a pen or pencil.
by: By means next to. You also use by to say who did something or how something is done.
going: Going is a form of the verb go. You use be going to to talk about what will happen.
along: If you move along a road or path, you move from one part of it towards the end.
near: If something is near a place, it is not far from it.
tenth: The tenth thing is the one that comes after the ninth.
king: A king is a man who rules a country and who comes from a royal family.
cover: If you cover something, you put something over it.
tip: The tip of something long and thin is the end of it. A tip is also a useful piece of advice.
height: The height of someone or something is how tall or high they are.
seal: A seal is a large animal with a smooth body and flippers that lives in the sea and on land.
nail: A nail is a thin, pointed piece of metal that you hit with a hammer. Your nails are also the hard parts at the ends of your fingers and toes.
hammer: A hammer is a tool with a heavy metal head and a handle. You use it to hit nails.
lizard: A lizard is a small reptile with four short legs and a long tail.
easy: Something that is easy is not difficult.
answer: An answer is what you say or write when someone asks you a question.
save: If you save someone, you help them to get away from danger. If you save money, you keep it to use later.
proud: If you are proud, you feel pleased about something good that you or someone close to you has done.
sight: Sight is the ability to see. A sight is also something that you see.
honey: Honey is a sweet, sticky food that bees make.
forgive: If you forgive someone who has done something wrong, you stop being angry with them.
jar: A jar is a glass container with a lid, used for keeping food such as jam.
obey: If you obey someone, you do what they tell you to do.
than: You use than when you compare two things.
before: If something happens before something else, it happens earlier.
half: A half is one of two equal parts of something.
sword: A sword is a weapon with a long metal blade and a handle.
bruise: A bruise is a purple or blue mark on your skin where you have been hit or have bumped into something.
honest: Someone who is honest tells the truth and does not steal or cheat.
between: If something is between two things, it has one on each side of it.
almost: Almost means very nearly but not completely.
fight: When people or animals fight, they try to hurt each other.
deep: Something that is deep goes a long way down from the top.
stretch: When you stretch, you put your arms or legs out as far as you can.
punishment: A punishment is something unpleasant that someone has to do or have because they did something wrong.
whale: A whale is a very large sea animal that breathes air through a hole on the top of its head.
melt: When something melts, it turns into liquid because it gets warm.
most: You use most to talk about the largest amount, or to say that something is more than all the others.
pay: When you pay for something, you give money to buy it.
quickly: If you do something quickly, you do it fast.
spring: Spring is the season after winter and before summer, when plants start to grow.
smart: Someone who is smart is clever. If you look smart, you are clean and well dressed.
lovely: Someone or something that is lovely is very nice or beautiful.
slowly: If you do something slowly, you do it without hurrying.
sparrow: A sparrow is a small brown bird that is common in towns and gardens.
hood: A hood is the part of a coat that you can pull up to cover your head.
thankful: If you are thankful, you are glad and grateful about something.
bake: When you bake, you cook food such as bread or cakes in an oven.
cloudy: If it is cloudy, there are a lot of clouds in the sky.
sprinkle: If you sprinkle something, you scatter small pieces or drops of it over something else.
eyebrow: Your eyebrows are the lines of hair above your eyes.
that: You use that to talk about a person or thing that is not near you.
check: If you check something, you look at it carefully to make sure it is right or safe.
ready: If you are ready, you are prepared to do something.
hate: If you hate something, you dislike it very much.
husband: A woman's husband is the man she is married to.
shoot: If you shoot in a game such as football, you kick or throw the ball towards the goal.
bone: A bone is one of the hard white parts inside your body that make up your skeleton.
chase: If you chase someone, you run after them to try to catch them.
pine: A pine is a tall tree with long, thin leaves like needles that stay green all year.
purse: A purse is a small bag that you keep your money in.
leap: If you leap, you jump high or a long way.
sickness: Sickness is the state of being ill.
holy: Something that is holy is special because it is connected with God or a religion.
dear: You write Dear at the start of a letter, before the name of the person you are writing to. Dear also means loved very much.
howl: If a dog or wolf howls, it makes a long, loud crying sound.
buy: If you buy something, you pay money to get it.
terrible: Something that is terrible is very bad.
bend: When you bend something, you make it curved. When you bend down, you move the top of your body towards the ground.
over: If something is over something else, it is above it. If you go over something, you cross it.
foal: A foal is a very young horse.
left: Your left side is the side of your body that most people do not write with.
none: None means not one or not any.
leave: When you leave a place, you go away from it.
list: A list is a set of words or names that you write one under the other.
In the KJV it can also mean: wish; please (원하다).
double: Something that is double is twice as big or has two parts.
weak: Someone who is weak is not strong.
dragon: A dragon is a large animal in stories that has wings and breathes fire.
poison: Poison is something that makes people or animals very ill or kills them if they eat or drink it.
stir: When you stir a liquid, you move it round with a spoon.
forehead: Your forehead is the part of your face above your eyes.
dangerous: Something that is dangerous could hurt you.
frozen: Something that is frozen has become ice, or is very cold.
return: If you return, you come back or go back. If you return something, you give it back.
thick: Something that is thick is wide from one side to the other. A thick liquid does not flow easily.
smooth: Something that is smooth has no lumps or rough parts.
bucket: A bucket is a round container with a handle, used for carrying water or sand.
sharpen: If you sharpen something, you make its point or edge sharp.
same: If two things are the same, they are exactly like each other.
friendship: Friendship is the feeling that friends have for each other.
nod: If you nod, you move your head up and down to show that you agree or understand.
remember: If you remember something, you keep it in your mind or bring it back into your mind.
view: The view from a place is everything that you can see from there.
fan: A fan is a machine with blades that spin round to make the air cooler. A fan is also someone who likes a person or team very much.
male: A male person or animal belongs to the sex that cannot have babies or lay eggs.
wake: When you wake, you stop sleeping.
pole: A pole is a long, thin stick of wood or metal. The North Pole and the South Pole are the most northern and southern points of the Earth.
mighty: Something that is mighty is very big and strong.
stack: A stack of things is a neat pile of them.
may: You use may to say that something might happen. You also use may to ask or give permission politely.
care: If you care about someone or something, you think they are important. If you care for someone, you look after them.
mule: A mule is an animal whose mother is a horse and whose father is a donkey.
cost: If something costs an amount of money, you have to pay that much to buy it.
space: Space is the area outside the Earth where the stars and planets are. A space is also an empty area.
wife: A man's wife is the woman he is married to.
fair: Something that is fair is right and the same for everyone. Fair hair is light in colour.
enter: If you enter a place, you go into it.
promise: If you promise to do something, you say that you will really do it.
remove: If you remove something, you take it away.
adventure: An adventure is an exciting experience that you have, often in a new place.
basket: A basket is a container made of thin strips of wood or plastic woven together.
oven: An oven is a box with a door that you heat to cook food.
skirt: A skirt is a piece of clothing worn by women and girls that hangs down from the waist.
send: If you send something, you make it go to another place, for example by post or email.
flat: A flat is a home with all its rooms on one floor of a bigger building.
fed: Fed is the past tense of feed.
bracelet: A bracelet is a chain or band that you wear round your wrist.
vomit: If you vomit, food comes up from your stomach and out of your mouth. It is also called being sick.
dishonest: Someone who is dishonest does not tell the truth or cheats.
den: A den is the home of a wild animal such as a fox. A den is also a secret place that children make to play in.
hairy: Something that is hairy is covered in hair.
helmet: A helmet is a strong, hard hat that keeps your head safe.
beautiful: Someone or something that is beautiful is very nice to look at.
meeting: A meeting is when people come together to talk about something.
spread: If you spread something, you put it in a thin layer over something.
anchor: An anchor is a heavy metal hook on a chain that you drop into the water to stop a boat from moving.
sunrise: Sunrise is the time in the morning when the sun first appears.
cucumber: A cucumber is a long, thin green vegetable that you eat raw in salads.
large: Something that is large is big.
fit: If you are fit, your body is healthy and strong because you exercise.
sport: A sport is a game such as football, tennis or swimming.
lock: A lock is a thing on a door, box or gate that keeps it shut. You need a key to open it.
beast: A beast is a large, wild or frightening animal.
warn: If you warn someone, you tell them about a danger or a problem.
crow: A crow is a large black bird.
cane: A cane is a long, thin stick. Some people use a cane to help them walk.
moth: A moth is an insect like a butterfly that usually flies at night.
robber: A robber is a person who steals things.
couple: A couple is two people who are married or in love. A couple of things means two or a few of them.
enjoy: If you enjoy something, you like doing it.
plenty: Plenty means a lot, or as much as you need.
find: If you find something that was lost, you see it after looking for it.
again: If something happens again, it happens one more time.
believe: If you believe something, you think that it is true.

lose: If you lose something, you cannot find it. If you lose a game, you do not win it.
camp: A camp is a place where people stay in tents or huts for a short time.

bare: If a part of your body is bare, it is not covered by clothes. A bare room has nothing in it.

rash: A rash is an area of red spots on your skin.
grasshopper: A grasshopper is an insect with long back legs that can jump high.
month: A month is one of the twelve parts of a year, such as January or May.
visit: If you visit someone or somewhere, you go to see them.
glad: If you are glad, you are happy about something.
channel: A channel is a television station. The English Channel is the sea between England and France.
quarter: A quarter is one of four equal parts of something.
pray: When people pray, they speak to God.
shine: When the sun or a light shines, it gives out bright light.
pile: A pile of things is a lot of them on top of each other.
darling: You call someone darling to show that you love them.
snail: A snail is a small, slow animal with a soft body and a shell on its back.
clear: Something that is clear is easy to see through, or easy to understand.
castle: A castle is a large, strong building with thick walls and towers, built long ago to keep people safe.
breath: Your breath is the air that goes in and out of your body when you breathe.
horrible: Something that is horrible is very bad or very unpleasant.
through: If you go through something, you go into it at one side and come out of it at the other side.
join: If you join a group or club, you become a member of it. If you join two things, you fix them together.
marry: When two people marry, they become partners for life in a special ceremony.
craft: A craft is making things with your hands, such as models or pottery.
eagle: An eagle is a large bird with a curved beak and strong claws that hunts small animals.
sack: A sack is a large bag made of strong cloth or paper.
cause: To cause something means to make it happen.
shot: A shot is when you kick, hit or throw a ball to try to score. A shot is also the firing of a gun.
safety: Safety is being safe from danger.
wide: Something that is wide is a long way from one side to the other.
evening: The evening is the part of the day between the afternoon and the night.
lay: If you lay something somewhere, you put it down carefully. When a bird lays an egg, the egg comes out of its body.
sentence: A sentence is a group of words that begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.
nurse: A nurse is a person whose job is to look after people who are ill or hurt, usually in a hospital.
fever: If you have a fever, your body is too hot because you are ill.
sore: If part of your body is sore, it hurts.
carriage: A carriage is one of the long parts of a train where people sit. In the past, a carriage was a vehicle pulled by horses.
become: If someone becomes something, they start to be it.
hour: An hour is a length of time. There are sixty minutes in an hour.
partner: Your partner is the person you are working or playing with. Someone's partner is also the person they live with or are married to.
weeds: Weeds are wild plants that grow where you do not want them, for example in a garden.
work: When you work, you do a job, or you try hard to do something. If a machine works, it does what it should.
tortoise: A tortoise is a slow animal with a hard shell on its back.
life: Your life is the time when you are alive.
under: If something is under something else, it is below it.
until: If something happens until a time, it goes on up to that time and then stops.
doing: Doing is a form of the verb do.
thought: A thought is an idea that you have in your mind. Thought is also the past tense of think.
west: West is the direction where the sun goes down in the evening.
female: A female person or animal belongs to the sex that can have babies or lay eggs.
quick: Something that is quick happens fast or takes a short time.

twice: If something happens twice, it happens two times.
furniture: Furniture is the large things in a home, such as tables, chairs, beds and cupboards.
noon: Noon is twelve o'clock in the middle of the day.
manners: Manners are polite ways of behaving, such as saying please and thank you.
shave: When someone shaves, they cut hair off their face or body with a razor.
lump: A lump is a small, solid piece of something. A lump is also a small swelling on your body.
ape: An ape is a large animal like a monkey but with no tail, such as a gorilla or a chimpanzee.
paw: A paw is the foot of an animal such as a cat or dog.
travel: If you travel, you go from one place to another, often far away.
ninth: The ninth thing is the one that comes after the eighth.
together: If people do something together, they do it with each other.
themselves: You use themselves when the people who do something are also the people it happens to.
weather: The weather is what it is like outside, for example whether it is sunny, rainy, hot or cold.
pair: A pair is two things of the same kind that go together.
root: A root is the part of a plant that grows under the ground and takes in water.
mint: Mint is a plant with a fresh, strong taste. A mint is also a sweet with this taste.
ruler: A ruler is a long, flat piece of plastic, wood or metal with straight edges, used for measuring and drawing straight lines.
scent: A scent is a pleasant smell.
lord: In capitals, LORD stands for God's personal name in Hebrew.
busy: If you are busy, you have a lot of things to do. A busy place is full of people.
innocent: If someone is innocent, they have not done anything wrong.
pot: A pot is a deep, round container used for cooking or for keeping things in.
brake: A brake is a part of a vehicle that makes it slow down or stop.

builder: A builder is a person whose job is to build or repair houses.
lid: A lid is the top of a box, pot or jar that you can take off.
sparkle: If something sparkles, it shines with lots of small points of light.
flake: A flake is a small, thin piece of something.
after: If something happens after something else, it happens later.
any: You use any in questions and negatives to mean some or none of something.
should: You use should to say what is the right thing to do.
few: A few means a small number of. Few means not many.
set: If you set something somewhere, you put it there. If you set the table, you put knives, forks and plates on it.
deal: A deal is an agreement. A great deal means a lot.
march: March is the third month of the year.
force: Force is strength or power. A force is a push or a pull.
race: A race is a competition to see who is the fastest.
daily: Something that is daily happens every day.
wedding: A wedding is a ceremony when two people get married.
fail: If you fail, you do not succeed in doing something.
anger: Anger is the strong feeling you have when you are cross about something.
odd: Something that is odd is strange. An odd number cannot be divided by two, such as 1, 3 and 5.
palm: Your palm is the inside of your hand. A palm is also a tall tree with big leaves at the top that grows in hot places.
quietly: If you do something quietly, you do it without making much noise.
cord: A cord is a strong, thick string. A cord is also an electric wire.
rub: If you rub something, you move your hand or a cloth backwards and forwards over it.
wax: Wax is a soft substance that melts when it is hot. Candles are made of wax.
wardrobe: A wardrobe is a tall cupboard where you hang your clothes.
hedge: A hedge is a row of bushes growing close together, often round a garden or field.
badger: A badger is a wild animal with a black and white striped face. It lives under the ground and comes out at night.
season: A season is one of the four parts of the year: spring, summer, autumn and winter.
hearing: Hearing is the sense that lets you hear sounds.
length: The length of something is how long it is.
kingdom: A kingdom is a country that has a king or queen.
stole: Stole is the past tense of steal.
eighth: The eighth thing is the one that comes after the seventh.
goodness: Goodness is being kind and good. People say "My goodness!" when they are surprised.
onion: An onion is a round vegetable with a strong smell and taste. It can make your eyes water when you cut it.
peel: If you peel fruit or vegetables, you take off their skin.
sew: When you sew, you join pieces of cloth together with a needle and thread.
south: South is the direction that is opposite north. In Britain, the sun is in the south at midday.
imagine: If you imagine something, you make a picture of it in your mind.
captain: The captain of a ship or plane is the person in charge of it. The captain of a team leads the team.
copy: If you copy something, you make or do something exactly the same as it.
hunt: When animals or people hunt, they chase and catch animals for food. If you hunt for something, you look for it.
twin: Twins are two children who have the same mother and were born on the same day.
treasure: Treasure is gold, silver, jewels or other valuable things.
hunger: Hunger is the feeling you have when you need food.
pill: A pill is a small, round piece of medicine that you swallow.
thirst: Thirst is the feeling that you need to drink something.
arrow: An arrow is a thin stick with a sharp point that you shoot from a bow. An arrow is also a sign like this → that shows a direction.
as: You use as to compare things, or to say that something happens while something else happens.
live: If you live somewhere, that is where your home is. If you live, you are alive.
field: A field is an area of land with grass or crops growing on it, often with a fence or hedge around it.
felt: Felt is the past tense of feel. Felt is also a thick, soft cloth.
meaning: The meaning of a word is what it means.
ornament: An ornament is a small, pretty thing that you put in a room or on a Christmas tree.
poor: Someone who is poor has very little money. You also say poor when you feel sorry for someone.
rose: A rose is a flower with a lovely smell and sharp thorns on its stem.
wild: Wild animals and plants live in nature, not with people.
path: A path is a narrow way that people walk along.
warning: A warning is something that tells you about a danger.
crash: A crash is an accident when a vehicle hits something. A crash is also a sudden loud noise.
permission: If you have permission to do something, someone has said that you can do it.
speaker: A speaker is a person who is speaking. A speaker is also the part of a radio or computer that the sound comes out of.

spoke: Spoke is the past tense of speak.

bored: If you are bored, you are tired and unhappy because you have nothing interesting to do.
flame: A flame is the hot, bright light that comes from a fire.
always: If something always happens, it happens every time.
lot: A lot means a large number or amount.
order: The order of things is the way they are arranged, one after another. An order is also something that someone tells you to do.
calm: If you are calm, you are not worried or excited. Calm water is still.
arrive: When you arrive somewhere, you get there.
hook: A hook is a curved piece of metal or plastic that you hang things on.
charming: Someone or something that is charming is very pleasant and attractive.
kindness: Kindness is being kind to others.
wizard: A wizard is a man in stories who can do magic.
pilgrim: A pilgrim is a person who goes on a long journey to a holy place.
either: Either means one or the other of two things.
opening: An opening is a hole or gap. The opening of something is the start of it.
engine: An engine is a machine that makes a car, train or plane move.
forest: A forest is a large area with lots of trees growing close together.
imagination: Your imagination is the part of your mind that makes up pictures and ideas.

bury: If you bury something, you put it in a hole in the ground and cover it with earth.

shovel: A shovel is a tool like a spade with a wide blade for moving earth, snow or coal.
twig: A twig is a small, thin branch of a tree.
record: A record is information that is written down and kept. A record is also the best result ever.
handle: A handle is the part of something that you hold, such as a cup, bag or door.
limit: A limit is the largest amount or the furthest point that is allowed.
spoil: If you spoil something, you make it less good. If you spoil a child, you give them everything they want.

rib: Your ribs are the curved bones round your chest.
stormy: When it is stormy, there is a lot of wind and rain.
title: The title of a book, film or song is its name.

unite: If people unite, they join together.
hail: Hail is small balls of ice that fall from the sky like rain.
launch: If you launch a boat, you put it into the water. If you launch a rocket, you send it into the sky.
valley: A valley is low land between hills or mountains.
deserve: If you deserve something, you should have it because of what you have done.
object: An object is a thing that you can see and touch.
childhood: Your childhood is the time when you are a child.
inner: Inner means inside, or close to the centre.
drought: A drought is a long time with no rain.
moment: A moment is a very short time.
northern: Northern means in or from the north.
pure: Something that is pure is not mixed with anything else.
monthly: Something that is monthly happens once a month.
praise: If you praise someone, you say that they have done something well.
copper: Copper is a reddish-brown metal. Coins and wires are often made of copper.
spark: A spark is a tiny piece of fire that flies out from something burning.
against: If you are against something, you do not agree with it. If something is against something else, it is touching it.
service: A service is a job that helps people, such as the bus service. A service is also a religious ceremony.
revenge: Revenge is hurting someone because they hurt you.
overcome: If you overcome a problem, you find a way to deal with it.
examination: An examination is an exam, a test of what you know. An examination is also a careful look at something.
spy: A spy is a person who secretly finds out information about another country or group.
prisoner: A prisoner is a person who is kept in prison.
yield: If something yields, it gives or produces something.
remainder: The remainder is the part that is left. In maths, a remainder is the number left over when one number does not divide exactly into another.
ferry: A ferry is a boat that carries people and cars across water.
salmon: A salmon is a large fish with pink flesh.
steep: A steep hill or slope rises sharply.
creep: If you creep, you move slowly and quietly.
confused: If you are confused, you do not understand something.
general: General means about the main parts, not the details. General also means for most people.
particular: Particular means one specific thing and not another.
host: A host is a person who invites guests and looks after them. A host is also the person who presents a TV show.
In the KJV it can also mean: army; great number (군대, 무리). "the LORD of hosts" = the LORD of armies.
guilty: If you feel guilty, you feel bad because you have done something wrong.
tradition: A tradition is something that people have done for a long time.
visible: Something that is visible can be seen.
angle: An angle is the space between two lines that meet. Angles are measured in degrees.
dull: Something that is dull is boring. A dull colour is not bright.
security: Security is things that keep a place or person safe.
mention: If you mention something, you talk about it briefly.
proof: Proof is something that shows that something is true.
device: A device is a machine or tool that does a special job.
polish: If you polish something, you rub it to make it clean and shiny.
fig: A fig is a soft, sweet fruit full of tiny seeds.
wool: Wool is the soft hair of sheep. It is used to make thread and clothes.
charm: Charm is a quality that makes people like you. A charm is also a small object on a bracelet, or a magic spell.
post: Post is the letters and parcels that are delivered to your home. A post is also a strong pole fixed in the ground.
receive: If you receive something, you get it.
purchase: If you purchase something, you buy it.
unknown: Something that is unknown is not known.
passage: A passage is a long, narrow space between walls. A passage is also a short part of a book.
mixture: A mixture is things that are mixed together.
delighted: If you are delighted, you are very happy about something.
ourselves: You use ourselves when the people who do something are you and others, and it happens to you too.
failing: A failing is a weakness or fault.
keeper: A keeper is a person who looks after animals in a zoo. In football, a keeper is a goalkeeper.
dismiss: If you dismiss people, you tell them that they can go.
agreement: An agreement is a decision or plan that two or more people agree on.
exact: Something that is exact is completely correct.
defend: If you defend someone or something, you protect them from attack.
occasion: An occasion is a time when something happens, especially something special.
succeed: If you succeed, you do what you were trying to do.
stiff: Something that is stiff is hard to bend or move.
remain: If you remain somewhere, you stay there.
mill: A mill is a building with a machine for grinding grain into flour. A mill is also a factory.
pipe: A pipe is a long tube that water or gas flows through.
tribe: one of the twelve families of Israel
lasting: Something that is lasting goes on for a long time.
transform: If you transform something, you change it completely.
commander: A commander is an officer in charge of a group of soldiers or a ship.
folk: Folk are people. Folk music is traditional music from a country.
instructor: An instructor is a person who teaches a skill, such as driving or swimming.
member: A member is a person who belongs to a group or club.
certain: If you are certain, you are completely sure.
fashion: Fashion is the style of clothes, hair and other things that are popular at a time.
delicate: Something that is delicate is easily broken or damaged.
file: A file is a folder for keeping papers in. A file is also information stored on a computer.
pleasure: Pleasure is a feeling of happiness and enjoyment.
suppose: If you suppose something, you think it is likely. If you are supposed to do something, you should do it.
pace: Your pace is how fast you walk or run. A pace is also one step.
nursing: Nursing is the job of a nurse.
colony: A colony is a group of animals of the same kind that live together. A colony is also a country ruled by another country.
glorious: Something that is glorious is very beautiful or wonderful.
fare: A fare is the money that you pay to travel on a bus, train or plane.
grove: A grove is a small group of trees.
gap: A gap is a space between two things.
warrior: A warrior is a brave fighter.
account: An account is a report of something that happened. A bank account is an arrangement to keep your money in a bank.
ancient: Something that is ancient is very old, from thousands of years ago.
pleased: If you are pleased, you are happy about something.
settle: If you settle somewhere, you start living there. If you settle an argument, you end it.
eternal: Something that is eternal lasts for ever.
lodge: A lodge is a small house in the country, often used for holidays.
arch: An arch is a curved structure, often over a doorway or under a bridge.
term: A term is one of the parts that the school year is divided into. A term is also a word with a special meaning.
lack: A lack of something is not having it, or not having enough of it.
labour: Labour is hard work, especially with your body.
means: A means is a way of doing something.
otherwise: Otherwise means if not, or apart from that.
flesh: Flesh is the soft part of a body under the skin. The flesh of a fruit is the soft part inside.
reasonable: Something that is reasonable is fair and sensible.
memorial: A memorial is something, such as a statue, that helps people remember a person or event.
ram: A ram is a male sheep.
law: A law is a rule that everyone in a country must obey.
protection: Protection is keeping someone or something safe.
proceed: If you proceed, you continue or go forward.
invention: An invention is something new that someone has made or thought of.
wicked: Someone who is wicked is very bad and cruel.
exchange: If you exchange things, you give one and get another back.
whom: Whom is used instead of who as the object of a verb or after a preposition. It is quite formal.
desert: A desert is a large, dry area of land with very little rain and few plants.
spare: Something that is spare is extra and not being used.
altogether: Altogether means in total, or completely.
custom: A custom is something that people in a place usually do.
college: A college is a place where people study after they leave school.
content: If you are content, you are happy and satisfied.
purpose: The purpose of something is why it is done or made.
toll: A toll is money that you pay to use a road or bridge.
goddess: A goddess is a female god.
uncertain: If you are uncertain, you are not sure.
grind: If you grind something, you crush it into a powder.
shuttle: A shuttle is a bus, train or plane that goes regularly between two places. A space shuttle is a spacecraft.
envy: Envy is the feeling of wanting something that someone else has.
court: A court is a place where a judge decides if someone has broken the law. A court is also an area for playing sports such as tennis.
perform: If you perform, you act, sing, dance or play music for an audience.
portion: A portion is a part or amount of something, especially food for one person.
gravity: Gravity is the force that pulls things towards the Earth.
grief: Grief is great sadness, especially when someone dies.
shall: You use shall with I and we to make offers and suggestions.
opinion: Your opinion is what you think about something.
condition: The condition of something is how good or bad it is. A condition is also something that must happen first.
secure: Something that is secure is safe and firmly fixed.
faithful: Someone who is faithful is loyal and keeps their promises.
plea: A plea is a strong request for help.
empire: An empire is a group of countries ruled by one leader or one country.
weakness: Weakness is not being strong. Your weakness is something that you are not good at or cannot say no to.
according: According to someone means as they say.
former: Former means from an earlier time.
league: A league is a group of sports teams that play against each other.
lend: If you lend something to someone, you let them use it for a while.
monument: A monument is a building or statue that helps people remember a person or event.
governor: A governor is a person who controls a place or organisation. School governors help to run a school.
supreme: Supreme means the highest or greatest.
communication: Communication is sharing information, for example by talking, writing or signing.
stake: A stake is a pointed stick that you push into the ground.
government: The government is the group of people who run a country.
natural: Something that is natural is made by nature, not by people.
respect: Respect is a feeling that someone is important and should be treated well.
approach: If you approach something, you come near to it.
clearly: Clearly means in a way that is easy to see, hear or understand.
avoid: If you avoid something, you keep away from it.
encourage: If you encourage someone, you give them hope and help them to do something.
cottage: A cottage is a small house, usually in the countryside.
terrified: If you are terrified, you are very frightened.
roast: If you roast food, you cook it in an oven or over a fire.
support: If you support someone, you help them. If you support a team, you want them to win.
release: If you release someone or something, you let them go.
mount: If you mount a horse or bike, you get onto it.
affection: Affection is a feeling of liking or loving someone.
receipt: A receipt is a piece of paper that shows that you have paid for something.
confession: A confession is when you say that you have done something wrong.
intelligence: Intelligence is being clever and able to understand things.
profit: A profit is the money that you make when you sell something for more than it cost you.
naturally: Naturally means of course, or in a natural way.
pollution: Pollution is harmful substances that make air, water or land dirty.
liver: Your liver is a large organ in your body that cleans your blood.
decrease: If something decreases, it becomes smaller or less.
acceptance: Acceptance is agreeing to something or taking something that is offered. Acceptance is also being welcomed into a group.
compare: If you compare things, you look at how they are the same and different.
willing: If you are willing to do something, you are happy to do it.
conduct: If you conduct something, you organise it and do it. A conductor conducts an orchestra.
experiment: An experiment is a test that scientists do to find something out.
submit: If you submit something, you give it to someone so that they can look at it or judge it.
issue: An issue is a subject or problem that people talk about. An issue is also one copy of a magazine.
prevent: If you prevent something, you stop it from happening.
In the KJV it can also mean: go before (앞서다). In the KJV prevent means come before, not stop.
lively: Someone or something that is lively is full of energy.
advice: Advice is what you say to help someone decide what to do.
nor: You use nor after neither or not to add another negative idea.
champion: A champion is a person or team that wins a competition.
offence: An offence is a crime. If you take offence, you are upset by something.
poet: A poet is a person who writes poems.
owe: If you owe someone money, you need to pay it back to them.
register: A register is an official list of names. In British schools, teachers take the register to check who is there.
ordinary: Something that is ordinary is normal and not special.
encounter: An encounter is a meeting, especially one you did not expect.
strain: Strain is worry or pressure. A strain is also an injury caused by stretching a muscle too much.
plot: The plot of a story is what happens in it. A plot is also a secret plan.
aboard: If you are aboard a ship, train or plane, you are on it.
supposed: If something is supposed to happen, it should happen or it is expected.
require: If you require something, you need it.
bay: A bay is a part of the coast where the land curves inwards.
payment: A payment is an amount of money that you pay.
paradise: Paradise is a perfect, beautiful place.
gallery: A gallery is a building where people go to look at paintings and other art.
physician: A physician is a doctor. This word is quite formal.
urgent: Something that is urgent needs to be done immediately.
expect: If you expect something, you think it will happen.
licence: A licence is an official paper that gives you permission to do something. In British English, the noun is spelt licence and the verb is spelt license.
spiritual: Spiritual means to do with your mind and feelings, or with religion, rather than your body.
renewed: Something that is renewed has started again or has been made new.
correction: A correction is a change that makes something right.
fulfil: If you fulfil a promise or a dream, you do it or make it happen.
search: If you search for something, you look carefully for it.
armed: Someone who is armed is carrying a weapon.
organ: An organ is a part of your body that does a special job, such as your heart. An organ is also a large musical instrument with pipes.
hatred: Hatred is a very strong feeling of not liking someone or something.
pity: Pity is feeling sorry for someone. If something is a pity, it is a shame.
supply: A supply is an amount of something that you can use.
foreign: Something that is foreign comes from another country.
request: A request is when you ask for something politely.
witness: A witness is a person who sees something happen, such as a crime or an accident.
defeat: If you defeat someone, you win against them.
sake: If you do something for someone's sake, you do it to help them.
assist: If you assist someone, you help them.
wealth: Wealth is a lot of money or valuable things.
delay: A delay is when something happens later than planned.
disorder: A disorder is an illness. Disorder is also a lack of order, or a mess.
estimate: If you estimate something, you make a sensible guess about it.
convince: If you convince someone, you make them believe something.
beam: A beam is a line of light. A beam is also a long, thick bar of wood or metal that holds up a roof.
furious: If you are furious, you are extremely angry.
hospitality: Hospitality is being friendly and welcoming to guests.
doubt: Doubt is a feeling of not being sure.
sporting: Sporting means to do with sport.
inform: If you inform someone, you tell them something.
sincere: Someone who is sincere means what they say.
decay: If something decays, it slowly rots or falls apart.
description: A description says what something or someone is like.
express: If you express a feeling or idea, you show it or say it.
incredible: Something that is incredible is amazing or hard to believe.
bitter: Something that is bitter has a strong, sharp taste that is not sweet. Bitter also means very cold, or angry and upset.
appearance: Your appearance is the way you look. An appearance is also when someone comes to a place or event.
appetite: Your appetite is how much you want to eat.
rate: A rate is how fast something happens, or how often it happens.
ability: An ability is being able to do something.
reputation: Your reputation is what people think of you.
drag: If you drag something, you pull it along the ground.
ridge: A ridge is the long, narrow top of a hill or mountain.
judge: A judge is a person who decides cases in a court. A judge also decides who wins a competition.
scale: A scale is a set of marks for measuring. In music, a scale is a set of notes going up or down. The scale of something is how big it is.
examine: If you examine something, you look at it very carefully.
frontier: A frontier is a border between two countries. A frontier is also the edge of what is known.
fellow: Fellow means of the same group as you.
determine: If you determine something, you find it out or decide it.
rent: Rent is money that you pay to live in a house or flat that belongs to someone else.
suffer: If you suffer, you feel pain or unhappiness.
In the KJV it can also mean: allow (허락하다). "Suffer the little children to come unto me" = Let the children come to me.
endless: Something that is endless seems to go on for ever.
humble: Someone who is humble does not think they are better than other people.
advise: If you advise someone, you tell them what you think they should do. In British English, the verb is spelt advise and the noun is spelt advice.
occupy: If you occupy a place, you live in it or fill it. If something occupies you, it keeps you busy.
mankind: Mankind is all the people in the world.
stable: A stable is a building where horses are kept.
divorce: A divorce is when a marriage is ended by law.
mutual: Mutual means shared by two or more people.
bore: If something bores you, you find it dull.
current: Current means happening now. A current is also a flow of water, air or electricity.
tax: Tax is money that people pay to the government.
determination: Determination is not giving up even when something is hard.
intend: If you intend to do something, you plan to do it.
foolish: Someone who is foolish is silly and does not think carefully.
experience: Experience is knowledge or skill that you get from doing something. An experience is something that happens to you.
pride: Pride is a feeling of being pleased about something you have done. A pride is also a group of lions.
distant: Something that is distant is far away.
warfare: Warfare is fighting in a war.
wilderness: A wilderness is a wild area of land where nobody lives.
threaten: If you threaten someone, you say that you will hurt them. If something threatens something, it puts it in danger.
throughout: Throughout means all through, in every part or for the whole time.
especially: Especially means more than usually, or more than others.
bound: If something is bound to happen, it is certain to happen.
hire: If you hire something, you pay to use it for a short time. If you hire someone, you pay them to work for you.
lifetime: A lifetime is all the time that someone is alive.
publish: If someone publishes a book or magazine, they print it and sell it.
breed: A breed is a type of animal, such as a type of dog.
widow: A widow is a woman whose husband has died.
differ: If things differ, they are not the same.
amongst: Amongst means among. This form is used in British English.
ancestors: Your ancestors are the people in your family who lived a long time before you.
fierce: Something that is fierce is angry, wild or strong.
advanced: Something that is advanced is at a high level, or very modern.
joint: A joint is a place where two bones meet, such as your knee or elbow. A joint is also a large piece of meat.
severe: Something that is severe is very bad or serious.
forecast: A forecast is what someone thinks will happen, especially with the weather.
confirmation: Confirmation is a message that shows that something is definitely true or will happen.
brass: Brass is a shiny yellow metal. Brass instruments are musical instruments made of brass, such as trumpets.
compassion: Compassion is feeling sorry for people who are suffering and wanting to help them.
mock: If you mock someone, you laugh at them in an unkind way.
coral: Coral is a hard substance made by tiny sea animals. It forms colourful reefs in warm seas.
access: Access is a way of getting into a place, or the right to use something.
despite: Despite means even though something is true.
recommend: If you recommend something, you say that it is good.
protest: A protest is when people show that they strongly disagree with something.
ease: Ease is being easy. If you are at ease, you feel relaxed.
burden: A burden is something heavy that you carry, or a problem that you have to deal with.
acknowledge: If you acknowledge something, you agree that it is true. If you acknowledge someone, you show that you have seen them.
urge: If you urge someone to do something, you try hard to make them do it.
consist: If something consists of things, it is made of them.
haven: A haven is a safe, peaceful place.
region: A region is a large area of a country or the world.
shipping: Shipping is sending goods, especially by ship. Shipping is also the cost of sending something.
trial: A trial is when a court decides whether someone is guilty. A trial is also a test of something.
election: An election is when people vote to choose someone, such as a leader.
benefit: A benefit is something good that helps you.
presence: Your presence somewhere is your being there.
banner: A banner is a long piece of cloth with words or pictures on it.
voluntary: Something that is voluntary is done because you want to, not because you must, and often without pay.
striker: A striker is a football player whose main job is to score goals.
standard: A standard is a level of quality.
thus: Thus means so, or in this way. It is a formal word.
native: Your native country is the place where you were born. A native plant or animal grows or lives naturally in a place.
behalf: If you do something on behalf of someone, you do it for them.
apply: If you apply for something, you write to ask for it. If you apply something, you put it on.
bold: Someone who is bold is brave and confident. Bold writing has thick, dark letters.
shelter: A shelter is a place that protects you from danger or bad weather.
costly: Something that is costly costs a lot of money.
stock: Stock is the things that a shop has to sell. Stock is also a liquid made by boiling meat or vegetables, used in cooking.
desperate: If you are desperate, you are in a very difficult situation and will try anything. Desperate also means wanting something very much.
customs: Customs is the place at an airport or port where officers check what people are bringing into a country.
burial: A burial is putting a dead person in a grave.
stroke: If you stroke something, you move your hand gently over it.
success: Success is doing well or getting what you wanted.
diet: Your diet is the kind of food that you usually eat. If you are on a diet, you eat less or eat special food.
situation: A situation is what is happening at a particular time.
effect: An effect is a change that something causes.
cease: If something ceases, it stops. This is a formal word.
comparison: A comparison is looking at how things are the same and different.
confidence: Confidence is feeling sure that you can do something well.
resort: A resort is a place where people go on holiday.
resist: If you resist something, you stop yourself from doing it or you fight against it.
amber: Amber is a hard yellow-orange substance from trees. Amber is also the orange colour in traffic lights.
chamber: A chamber is a large room used for a special purpose.
tackle: If you tackle a problem, you deal with it. In football, if you tackle someone, you try to take the ball from them.
breeding: Breeding is when animals have babies, or when people keep animals to produce young.
advantage: An advantage is something that helps you to do better than others.
port: A port is a town by the sea where ships load and unload.
obtain: If you obtain something, you get it. This is a formal word.
rely: If you rely on someone or something, you need them and trust them.
consider: If you consider something, you think about it carefully.
confirm: If you confirm something, you say that it is definitely true or that it will happen.
refuse: If you refuse to do something, you say that you will not do it.
preparation: Preparation is getting ready for something.
invasion: An invasion is when an army goes into another country to take control of it.
kidney: Your kidneys are two organs in your body that clean your blood.
gulf: A gulf is a large area of sea that is partly surrounded by land.
intent: Intent is what you plan to do.
comparable: Things that are comparable are similar in size or quality.
conference: A conference is a large meeting where people talk about a subject.
dealer: A dealer is a person who buys and sells things.
convenient: Something that is convenient is useful and easy, or happens at a good time.
mere: Mere means only, or no more than.
rank: A rank is a position in an organisation, such as the army.
counsel: If you counsel someone, you give them advice about their problems.
reign: A reign is the time when a king or queen rules.
prey: Prey is an animal that is hunted and eaten by another animal.
madness: Madness is very silly or dangerous behaviour.
conclusion: A conclusion is the end of something. A conclusion is also a decision that you make after thinking.
composition: A composition is a piece of music or writing that someone has created.
cope: If you cope, you manage to deal with a difficult situation.
justice: Justice is fairness, or the system of laws that decides whether people are guilty.
extreme: Something that is extreme is very great or very strong.
reveal: If you reveal something, you let people see it or know about it.
permit: If you permit something, you allow it.
alter: If you alter something, you change it.
stern: Someone who is stern is serious and strict.
unity: Unity is being together or agreeing.
council: A council is a group of people chosen to run a town or city.
employment: Employment is having a paid job.
founder: A founder is a person who starts an organisation or business.
lieutenant: A lieutenant is an officer in the army or navy. In British English, it sounds like "left-tenant".
custody: If someone has custody of a child, they are legally in charge of looking after them. If the police take someone into custody, they keep them at a police station.
ignorant: If you are ignorant of something, you do not know about it.
generation: A generation is all the people born at about the same time. A generation is also a stage in a family, such as parents or grandparents.
satisfaction: Satisfaction is the good feeling when you have done something well or got what you wanted.
observe: If you observe something, you watch it carefully.
reject: If you reject something, you say no to it or do not accept it.
necessity: A necessity is something that you must have.
devoted: If you are devoted to someone or something, you love them very much.
debate: A debate is a discussion where people give their opinions about a subject.
dedication: Dedication is working very hard at something because it is important to you.
heir: An heir is a person who will receive money, property or a title when someone dies.
loan: A loan is money that you borrow and must pay back.
conflict: A conflict is a serious disagreement or a fight.
confident: If you are confident, you feel sure about yourself and your abilities.
cure: A cure is something that makes an illness go away.
excess: An excess is too much of something.
companion: A companion is someone you spend time with or travel with.
profession: A profession is a job that needs special training, such as being a doctor or a teacher.
dignity: Dignity is being calm, serious and worthy of respect.
affect: If something affects you, it changes you or has an effect on you.
infinite: Something that is infinite has no end or limit.
sincerely: If you say something sincerely, you really mean it. In Britain, Yours sincerely is used to end a letter to someone whose name you know.
ministry: A ministry is a government department. The ministry is also the work of a church minister.
wisdom: Wisdom is knowledge and good judgement that come from experience.
sacrifice: offering killed and given to God
ally: An ally is a person or country that supports another.
landmark: A landmark is a famous building or place that is easy to recognise.
fringe: A fringe is hair cut so that it hangs over your forehead. The fringe of something is its edge.
ought: You use ought to say what is the right thing to do.
In the KJV it can also mean: anything (in some verses) (무엇이든).
expert: An expert is a person who knows a lot about something.
preserve: If you preserve something, you keep it safe or stop it from changing.
direct: Something that is direct goes straight from one place to another without stopping. A direct person says what they think.
principle: A principle is a rule or belief that you follow.
satisfied: If you are satisfied, you are pleased with what you have got or done.
substance: A substance is a solid, a liquid or a gas.
partial: Something that is partial is not complete.
strengthen: If you strengthen something, you make it stronger.
observer: An observer is a person who watches something.
opportunity: An opportunity is a chance to do something.
depth: The depth of something is how deep it is.
conscience: Your conscience is the part of your mind that tells you whether something is right or wrong.
thrust: If you thrust something, you push it hard and suddenly.
decline: If something declines, it becomes less or smaller. If you decline something, you politely say no.
translation: A translation is something that has been changed from one language into another.
tend: If you tend to do something, you usually do it. If you tend something, you look after it.
heritage: Heritage is the history, traditions and buildings that a country or family has had for a long time.
consultation: A consultation is a meeting to talk about something or get advice, for example with a doctor.
struggle: If you struggle, you try very hard to do something difficult.
merchant: A merchant is a person who buys and sells goods, especially in the past.
acre: An acre is a unit for measuring land.
constant: Something that is constant happens all the time or does not change.

ye: you (more than one, as the subject)
